chunks: 1617 - And Muḥammad ibn Muslim narrated from him, peace be upon him, that he said:
A man said to him: A person sent the zakat of his wealth to be distributed, but it was lost. Is he liable for it until it is distributed?

He said: “If he found a proper place for it but did not hand it over, then he is liable for it until he delivers it. But if he did not find anyone to whom he could hand it over, and so he sent it to its rightful recipients, then there is no liability upon him for it, because it has left his possession.

And likewise the trustee to whom a bequest is entrusted is liable for what was delivered to him if he finds its owner, the one to whom he was commanded to deliver it. But if he does not find him, then there is no liability upon him.”

key_terms.الْوَصِيُّ: the trustee or executor entrusted with carrying out a bequest
key_terms.زَكَاةِ: zakat, the obligatory alms due from one's wealth
key_terms.ضَمَانُهَا: liability for compensation of the lost property
key_terms.مَوْضِعًا: a proper place or eligible outlet for distribution

ai.seo_question: Is a person liable if zakat is lost before it reaches its rightful recipients?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the legal ruling of liability regarding zakat that has been set aside for distribution. If a person delays payment despite having access to a rightful recipient, he remains liable; but if he sends it onward when no recipient is available to him, he is not liable once it leaves his hand. The same rule applies to a trustee or executor entrusted with property for delivery.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1617 - Muhammad ibn Muslim reported from him (Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as)) that

a man asked him about someone who sent the Zakat of his wealth to be distributed, but it was lost before being distributed.
The man asked: "Is he liable for it until it is distributed?"

The Imam (as) replied: "If he found someone to whom he could give it but did not hand it over, he is liable for it until he gives it. However, if he could not find someone to give it to and sent it to its rightful recipients, then he is not liable for it, as it has left his possession.

The same applies to a trustee (executor of a will) who is entrusted with something. If he finds the rightful owner to whom he was instructed to deliver it but does not hand it over, he is liable. However, if he cannot find the rightful owner, he is not liable."
